subject: Sandboxed gateway isolation — annotated walkthrough & evidence
messages:
From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@veridianhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: security.team@veridianhealth.com, procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: isolation walkthrough + evidence for Dedicated/Private

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this — Veridian is finalizing our SOC 2 scoping and we need a concise security architecture package focused on Dedicated/Private deployments. Specifically we are asking for:  
- An annotated network diagram showing the sandboxed gateway (ingress/egress), tenant demarcation, and control-plane endpoints.
- A short narrative (1–2 pages) describing how tenant isolation is enforced (L2/L3 overlays, sidecar vs host-based fences, KV cache access controls).
- Evidence mapping to CAIQ/SIG sections relevant to network isolation & control plane (a checklist is fine).

We attached our assessment request form (VERIDIAN_Security_Assessment_Request.pdf). Can you confirm what you can provide by end of week?

Regards,
Alice Tan
Security Architect — Veridian Health

[attachment: VERIDIAN_Security_Assessment_Request.pdf]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: isolation walkthrough + evidence for Dedicated/Private

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We've pulled together an initial package and a first-pass diagram attached. Highlights below; full notes attached (controlplane-segmentation-notes.pdf) and a PNG diagram (sandbox-gateway-diagram-v1.png).

Summary (TL;DR):
- Sandboxed gateway: stateless ingress gateway in customer VPC with strict ACLs and egress ACLs to a controlled NAT/collector. The gateway performs TLS termination and routes to per-tenant service rings via an overlay (VXLAN) that enforces tenant tagging.
- Tenant fencing: multi-layer isolation: 1) network overlay + per-tenant subnets; 2) service mesh sidecars enforce mTLS and RBAC; 3) runtime process namespace and seccomp profiles for Dedicated nodes.
- Control plane separation: control plane endpoints live in a private management VPC with VPC peering and solely mutual-TLS authenticated connections from dedicated compute; no public control endpoints for Private deployments.
- KV cache and artifacts: tenant-scoped encryption keys (KMS) and short-lived credentials; cache entries are keyed with tenant identifiers and are scoped by runtime ACLs.

Deliverables in this message:
- Annotated diagram (sandbox-gateway-diagram-v1.png) — shows overlay, gateway, egress collectors, and control-plane private endpoints.
- Technical narrative + CAIQ/SIG mapping (controlplane-segmentation-notes.pdf).
- Next steps: Marcus will update the diagram to show explicit VXLAN tag ranges and the egress proxy behavior; Kimberly will map the diagram elements to the exact CAIQ questions Veridian flagged.

We can provide a second revision with redlines by Wednesday EOD. If you need items broken into separate artifacts for your audit portal (diagram + checklist + packet capture sample), say so and we'll split them out.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Enterprise Sales (Technical Accounts)
Redwood Inference

[attachments: sandbox-gateway-diagram-v1.png; controlplane-segmentation-notes.pdf]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: isolation walkthrough + evidence for Dedicated/Private

Looping in a few small redlines on the draft before we send to Veridian:  
1) Diagram: show explicit CIDR ranges for management/control plane VPC vs tenant subnets (we should avoid revealing exact customer CIDRs — use ranges like 10.100.0.0/16 management; 10.200.0.0/16 tenants).
2) Overlay details: include a small legend that explains the VXLAN tag allocation and how tags map to tenant IDs (this is critical for SOC 2 network separation evidence).
3) Egress: clarify the NAT/proxy behavior and note that egress to third-party telemetry is blocked unless whitelisted per-customer.
4) CAIQ/SIG mapping: add explicit question IDs next to each diagram element (e.g., CAIQ_NET.1 -> gateway ACLs).

Marcus — can you produce a v2 diagram and a one-page redline response mapping by EOD Wednesday? I'll then produce a CAIQ mapping spreadsheet that references the diagram file.

Thanks — K
